title: Composite Materials
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner identifies composite materials in the locality (concrete and reinforced concrete, plywood, chipboard, hardboard, fibreglass, wattle and daub, mud blocks with straw), describes what each is made of (two or more materials combined), and relates them to uses (buildings, furniture, water tanks, boats).
representations: samples: plywood edge, chipboard, a concrete piece
steps: Say what it is made of.

board.do: Draw a cut concrete beam with steel bars near the bottom.
Wait for the learner to say to resist pulling or bending.
Write what each part of the composite adds.

misconceptions.repair: Mix a small batch: cement, sand, ballast and water; break an old piece to see the stones inside.

listen_for: From one solid piece of wood
misconceptions.repair: Look at the edge: thin layers (veneers) glued with the grain crossing, which makes it strong and stops splitting.

misconceptions.ask: What is reinforced concrete mainly used for?
misconceptions.repair: Visit or show a building site: beams, columns and slabs are reinforced concrete.

misconceptions.ask: Why are steel bars put inside concrete?
misconceptions.repair: Bend a thin slab of plain mortar until it cracks underneath; explain the steel goes where the pulling is.

checks.question: How is plywood made?
checks.answer: Thin layers of wood glued with the grain crossing
